title: Concise stream lifecycle and event bridge ergonomics for Python SDK
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: The current Python SDK streaming chat surface requires consumers to wire low-level event parsing, retry logic, and checkpointing in each app. This leads to duplicated code, subtle bugs around resumability and idempotency, and poor developer ergonomics for common patterns (interruptible UI streaming, durable checkpoints for long-running chats, and graceful backpressure handling).

Goal: Provide a concise, opinionated lifecycle API and an event-bridge helper that lets application code express intent (resume points, soft retries, commit semantics) without managing low-level SSE/websocket plumbing. The API should be:
- Minimal: 1-2 primitives for most use cases (sync/async iterators + optional handler hooks)
- Resumable: clear hooks for checkpointing KV cache and consumer-side offsets
- Safe: idempotent retry semantics for partial responses and replays
- Observable: expose telemetry hooks for incrementally emitted tokens and commit boundaries

This ticket covers design, an initial implementation in the Python SDK, tests, a small migration guide, and a short cookbook example for frontend developers integrating streaming chat with UI components.
acceptance_criteria: New high-level API available as redwood.streaming.ChatStream that provides an async iterator over typed events (token, delta, control) without requiring the user to manage raw SSE frames.
Built-in checkpoint() hook that returns an opaque resume token and an apply_resume(token) method to continue a stream from the last committed event.
Configurable retry policy (soft_retry with idempotency key, hard_retry) documented and exercised in unit tests covering partial response replay and duplicate suppression.
Backpressure example included: bounded queue example with drop/slowdown strategies and a recommended default for UIs.
End-to-end integration test that simulates connection interrupt and verifies client recovers and emits identical logical messages to the consumer (deduplicated).
Docs and 1-page migration guide in docs/streaming/upgrade-from-low-level.md plus a short example in examples/streaming-chat-ui.py.
PR reviewed by 2 engineers and sign-off from SDK lead and one product developer; metrics telemetry hook accepted by observability team.
tasks: Finalize API sketch and internal design doc (confluence: /display/SDK/Chat+Stream+Lifecycle).
Implement ChatStream high-level wrapper that yields objects with .type in {token, delta, meta} and .cursor for resume points.
Add checkpoint()/apply_resume() and idempotency-key plumbing to the runtime so backend knows safe replay boundaries.
Write unit tests for partial replay, duplicate suppression, and backpressure behavior.
Add an example integration (examples/streaming-chat-ui.py) showing UI hydration, pause/resume, and safe retry on transient failures.
Update SDK docs and add migration guide + quickstart in README.
Create e2e test harness that can inject connection failures and assert semantic equivalence after resume.
Ship behind feature flag (SDK config: streaming_experimental_v2) and rollout to beta customers for feedback.
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created by Alyssa. Initial problem statement and high-level goals added.

2026-02-23: Design review with runtime team. Decided to keep transport-agnostic surface (works for SSE and websocket). Marcus to prototype a small wrapper that maps wire events to typed StreamEvent objects.

2026-03-02: Prototype implemented. Found edge case: backend may deliver identical token fragments on replay; added dedupe by (idempotency_key, fragment_index) at client-side and contract with backend to provide stable fragment indices.
2026-03-05: UX meeting: agreed default backpressure strategy will be bounded queue with drop-old semantics and telemetry counter for dropped tokens. Added example in tasks.
2026-03-09: PR #6321 opened: initial implementation + tests. Requesting reviews from @sanjay, @tess and @leon. Observability hooks are minimal (emit stream_event and checkpoint_event).
2026-03-10: Addressed review feedback: renamed ResumeToken -> StreamCursor, simplified API to .checkpoint() returning string token, added apply_resume(token). Seeking SDK lead sign-off.
notes: Implementation choices considered: (1) keep callbacks-first model vs (2) iterator-first model. Chosen iterator-first for ergonomic async/await usage and easier composition with existing asyncio queues.
Telemetry: emit lightweight events (stream.start, token.emitted, checkpoint.created, stream.resume) and ensure each has trace_id to correlate with SDK traces.
Performance: minimal allocation on token emission path; reuse small buffer objects and avoid per-token coroutine scheduling where possible (use async generators that yield strings).

Open questions: long-running conversation storage strategy for resumes (KV size limits), whether to persist StreamCursor format for >1 year (compatibility), and whether to expose granular commit vs auto-commit controls.
